scores.evidence: The one figure (practice-flow, flowchart TD) renders cleanly at 390 px and 1440 px. Its JP labels (イベントの作成（幹事）→…→参加人数の一覧（幹事）) and EN labels are readable and in the right language, and it has a caption and a 図の説明を読む / Describe the figure in words toggle (mobile-jp-11/12, desktop-en-08). On mobile the four stacked boxes fill a whole screen with wide side margins (mobile-jp-11), which works but is not dense.

No screen is text-only (textOnlyScreens empty in all three shots). The page alternates steps with expected-result boxes, prompt cards, the checklist and quizzes, so no screen holds a wall of prose (mobile-jp-03 to -16). Desktop JP lines average 36 chars per line (target 30–40) and EN 69 (target 60–75).

The EN screenshots contain no leftover Japanese: prompt vars show 'goal', 'my sorting' and 'app name', the diagram labels are English, and the glossary chips read Talking it through / MoSCoW / One-page plan (desktop-en-05, -07, -08). Nothing is hidden under the mobile top or bottom bars, the quiz option boxes are large tap targets, and the diagram has alt text plus a text description.

niceToHave: hook-predict: on desktop JP the question wraps with a lone 「う？」 on the second line (desktop-jp-01). A slightly shorter prompt, e.g. 「幹事が機能を分け直すとき、AIの借り方として最も合うのはどれでしょう？」, would fit on one line at 680 px.
practice-prompt-interview: on mobile the line breaks inside 「1つず／つしてください」 (mobile-jp-05). This is acceptable for prompt text, but 「質問は1つずつしてください。」 as its own line would read better.
practice-flow: on mobile the diagram takes a full screen (mobile-jp-11). It is optional, but shorter labels with the role on the same line, e.g. 「イベント作成（幹事）」, would make the boxes less tall.
reader: on mobile the flashcard hint says 「クリックまたはスペースキーでめくる」 (mobile-jp-18). A touch device should say タップ instead.
reader: the left table of contents on desktop JP breaks 「演習3：1枚企画書にまと／めて直す」 mid-word (desktop-jp-06). Wrapping at phrase boundaries (word-break: auto-phrase) would avoid this.
summary: lessonHash sha256:7dfd5355b05405d5 matches metrics.json. There are no hard failures: no sideways overflow, console errors, mermaid errors, unknown blocks or broken images. Mobile, desktop JP and desktop EN all render cleanly. Steps, prompt cards, the TD flow diagram, the checklist and the quizzes break the page into readable chunks, and the EN version is fully localized. Nothing needs to be fixed; the remaining points are cosmetic line breaks and two reader-level tweaks.
